kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-01.title: Order by size
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-01.body:
The mushroom grows every day, so the smallest one is Monday and the biggest one is Friday. From smallest to biggest: (B), (E), (C), (A), (D). Tuesday is the second day, so it is the second smallest: (E).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-01.title: Just two steps
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-01.body:
Find the smallest mushroom: (B) — that's Monday. The next smallest is (E), with a cap just a little bigger. So Tuesday is (E).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-02.title: Match the neighbours
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-02.body:
Every tile of the wall has orange half-petals on its edges that join with the petals of the neighbouring tiles to make whole petals and 'flowers'. Look at the four tiles around the gap: the missing tile must continue all their half-petals, and it must also follow the same up-down and left-right pattern as the rest of its row and column. Only tile (E) has its petals in exactly those places.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-02.title: Copy from the same row
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-02.body:
The pattern repeats every two tiles. So the missing tile looks exactly like the tile two places to its left (or right) in the same row. That tile matches (E).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-03.title: Calculate every square
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-03.body:
- $16+4 = 20$ ✔
- $19+1 = 20$ ✔
- $28-8 = 20$ ✔
- $2\times 10 = 20$ ✔
- $16-4 = 12$ ✘
- $7\times 3 = 21$ ✘

The whole top row and the bottom-left square are shaded.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-03.title: Look for the wrong ones
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-03.body:
Find the squares that are **not** 20: $16-4=12$ and $7\times3=21$, the bottom middle and bottom right. Only (A) leaves exactly those two white.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-04.title: Count all, subtract those with the dot
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-04.body:
A $4\times4$ grid has $16$ small squares, $9$ squares of size $2\times2$, $4$ of size $3\times3$ and $1$ of size $4\times4$: $30$ squares in total.

The dot is in the second row, second column. Squares containing it: the $1\times1$ square itself (1), $2\times2$ squares: 4, $3\times3$ squares: all 4, and the big square: 1. That is $10$ squares.

$30 - 10 = 20$.

**Answer: (A) 20**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-04.title: Count directly by size
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-04.body:
- $1\times1$: 15 squares without the dot.
- $2\times2$: of the 9, only the 4 in the top-left corner area contain the dot, so 5 don't.
- $3\times3$: all 4 contain the dot, 0 don't.
- $4\times4$: contains the dot.

$15 + 5 = 20$.

**Answer: (A) 20**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-05.title: Count the white parts
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-05.body:
All five figures are the same $4\times4$ grid, so the one with the **least white** has the largest shaded part. A white triangle is half a square.

- (A): 2 white squares + 2 half squares = 3 squares
- (B): 3 squares + 1 half = 3½
- (C): 2 squares + 3 halves = 3½
- (D): 3 squares + 1 half = 3½
- (E): 7 halves = 3½

(A) has the least white.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-05.title: Count the shaded parts
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-05.body:
Out of 16 squares, (A) has $16 - 3 = 13$ squares shaded, and each of the others has $16 - 3\tfrac12 = 12\tfrac12$.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-06.title: Rule out the neighbours
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-06.body:
A face is never opposite a face that touches it. In the first picture the duck touches the mouse and the ladybug. In the second picture the duck touches the elephant and the dog. So the duck touches mouse, ladybug, elephant and dog. The only sticker left is the **fly**, which must be opposite the duck.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-06.title: Each face has four neighbours
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-06.body:
Every face of a cube touches 4 faces and is opposite 1. We already found 4 neighbours of the duck (mouse, ladybug, elephant, dog), so the last sticker, the fly, is opposite.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-07.title: Try to use many small pieces
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-07.body:
The grid has 17 squares. To use many pieces, use the small ones: $1+2+3+4+5 = 15$, and with a sixth piece we would need at least $15 + 6 = 21 > 17$. So 6 pieces are impossible.

5 pieces work: $1+2+3+4+7 = 17$.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-07.title: Check from the top
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-07.body:
7 pieces: $1+2+\dots+7 = 28$, too many. 6 pieces: the smallest six give $1+2+3+4+5+6 = 21$, still more than 17. 5 pieces: $1+2+3+4+7=17$ fits exactly.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-08.title: Count the boxes that are used
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-08.body:
Boxes with a pencil: 5. Boxes with an eraser: 4. Two boxes are counted twice (they have both). So the number of boxes with something in them is $5 + 4 - 2 = 7$. Empty boxes: $10 - 7 = 3$.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-08.title: Sort the boxes
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-08.body:
- Pencil and eraser: 2 boxes
- Only a pencil: $5 - 2 = 3$ boxes
- Only an eraser: $4 - 2 = 2$ boxes

That is $2+3+2 = 7$ boxes used, so 3 are empty.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-09.title: Each region touches the two before it
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-09.body:
Number the regions from the outside in: 1 (outer ring), 2 (band at the top), 3 (band at the bottom), 4, 5, 6 and 7 (the small oval). Each region touches the two regions just before it, so any three neighbours in this list need three different colours. The colours must go red, blue, yellow, red, blue, yellow, red (or with blue and yellow swapped). Red regions: 1, 4 and 7 — that is **3** regions.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-09.title: Every third region
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-09.body:
Since regions 1, 2, 3 all touch each other, they use all three colours. Region 4 touches 2 and 3, so it gets the colour of region 1 (red); region 7 likewise. So red is used for every third region: 1, 4, 7.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-10.title: List by type
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-10.body:
Years with exactly two zeros:

- 2001 to 2009: zeros in the middle (2**00**x) — 9 years.
- 2010, 2020, ..., 2090: 2**0**x**0** — 9 years.
- 2100 — 1 year.

Total $9 + 9 + 1 = 19$.

**Answer: (E) 19**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-10.title: Where is the second zero?
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-10.body:
Every year 20xy from 2001 to 2099 already has one zero (the second digit). It needs exactly one more zero among $x$ and $y$: either $x = 0$, $y \ne 0$ (2001–2009, 9 years) or $y = 0$, $x\ne 0$ (2010–2090, 9 years). Then add 2100. $9+9+1 = 19$.

**Answer: (E) 19**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-11.title: Count the pieces of the fence
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-11.body:
In the 4-metre fence there are 5 upright posts, each made of 2 poles (10 poles), and 2 horizontal rails, each made of 4 poles (8 poles): 18 poles.

A 10-metre fence has 11 upright posts: $11\times 2 = 22$ poles, and 2 rails of 10 poles: 20 poles. Total $22 + 20 = 42$.

**Answer: (E) 42**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-11.title: Each metre adds the same
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-11.body:
Every extra metre of fence needs 2 more rail poles and one more post of 2 poles: 4 poles per metre. Start: one post (2 poles), then each metre adds 4. For 10 metres: $2 + 10\times 4 = 42$ (check: for 4 metres $2 + 16 = 18$, as in the picture).

**Answer: (E) 42**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-12.title: Together they cover 10 steps
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-12.body:
The kangaroo starts at the bottom and the rabbit at step 100. Each move, the distance between them shrinks by $7 + 3 = 10$ steps. They start 100 steps apart, so they meet after $100\div 10 = 10$ moves. Then the kangaroo has gone up $10\times 7 = 70$ steps, and the rabbit is at $100 - 30 = 70$ too.

**Answer: (D) 70**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-12.title: Table
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-12.body:
Kangaroo: 7, 14, 21, ..., 70. Rabbit: 97, 94, 91, ..., 70. After the 10th move both are on step 70.

**Answer: (D) 70**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-13.title: Follow the pattern
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-13.body:
Each token touches its two neighbours, and between those two shared triangles there is one triangle on the inside of the crown. Look at the bottom token: it touches its left neighbour with 1, has 5 inside and touches its right neighbour with 4. The next token touches with 4, has 3 inside and passes on 2; the next one touches with 2, has 1 inside and passes on 5, and so on. The numbers go down by one each step, so the tokens repeat after 5 tokens.

The crown has 10 tokens, so the top token is exactly like the bottom token, turned half way round. The triangle X is where the bottom token touches its right neighbour, turned around: the **4**.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-13.title: Turn the picture
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-13.body:
Because 10 tokens = 2 × 5 and the pattern repeats every 5 tokens, the crown looks the same after half a turn. Turning the picture upside down moves X onto the bottom token's triangle with the number 4 (the one it shares with its right neighbour).

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-14.title: Find the secret number
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-14.body:
The results add up to $24 + 13 + 7 = 44$. The original numbers add up to 50, so the secret number was subtracted three times for a total of $50 - 44 = 6$: the secret number is 2. The original numbers are 26, 15 and 9. Only 9 is a choice.

**Answer: (A) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-14.title: Test the choices
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-14.body:
If 9 is an original number, the secret number is $9 - 7 = 2$ and the numbers are 26, 15, 9 with sum 50 ✔. (If 11 were one, it would give 7 → secret 4, numbers 28, 17, 11 with sum 56 ✘, and so on.)

**Answer: (A) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-15.title: Find the repeating pattern
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-15.body:
The pattern repeats every 3 rows: rows 1, 4, 7 look the same, rows 2, 5, 8 look the same and rows 3, 6, 9 look the same. Using the complete rows at the top, fill in the missing tiles of rows 6 to 9 and count the dot tiles among them:

- row 6: 1 dot tile missing
- row 7: 1 dot tile missing
- row 8: 2 dot tiles missing
- row 9: 2 dot tiles missing

Total $1+1+2+2 = 6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-15.title: Count by columns
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-15.body:
The columns also repeat every 3 columns. Copy each missing tile from the tile 3 rows above it (which is the same). Doing this for all the gaps gives 6 dot tiles.

**Answer: (C) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-16.title: Try numbers of 6-member teams
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-16.body:
Take away 6-member teams until what is left can be split into 5s:

- 0 teams of 6: 43 (not a multiple of 5)
- 1: 37 ✘
- 2: 31 ✘
- 3: 25 = 5 teams of 5 ✔

So there are $3 + 5 = 8$ teams.

**Answer: (D) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-16.title: Use the limits
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-16.body:
With 7 teams there are at most $7\times6 = 42 < 43$ people, too few. With 9 teams there are at least $9\times 5 = 45 > 43$, too many. So there are 8 teams (5 of 5 and 3 of 6).

**Answer: (D) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-17.title: Four rolls bring it back
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-17.body:
At the start the top shows 1, the front 2 and the right side 3 (so the left side is 4). The die rolls to the right 5 times. Rolling 4 times in the same direction turns it all the way round, back to the start position. So only one roll really matters.

After one roll to the right: the old left face (4) comes on top, the old top (1) goes to the right side, and the front stays 2. Total $4 + 1 + 2 = 7$.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-17.title: Roll it step by step
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-17.body:
Track (top, right) with the front always 2: (1, 3) → (4, 1) → (6, 4) → (3, 6) → (1, 3) → (4, 1). The three faces show $4 + 1 + 2 = 7$.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-18.title: Start with vanilla
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-18.body:
The three vanilla scoops must all have different toppings, so they get a cherry, a wafer and the chocolate chip. Left: 2 cherries and 1 wafer. The two chocolate scoops must be different, so one gets a cherry and one the wafer. The lemon scoop gets the last cherry.

So lemon always gets a cherry: lemon with a wafer is impossible.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-18.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-18.body:
In the only possible arrangement — vanilla: cherry, wafer, chip; chocolate: cherry, wafer; lemon: cherry — (A), (B), (D) and (E) all appear, but (C) lemon with a wafer does not.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-19.title: Use the total
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-19.body:
$1 + 2 + \dots + 8 = 36$. Triangles and squares together cover $10 + 20 = 30$, so the circle covers $36 - 30 = 6$.

**Answer: (D) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-19.title: Find the shapes
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-19.body:
Four different numbers from 1–8 with sum 10 must be $1+2+3+4$. The squares use three of 5, 6, 7, 8 with sum 20: $5+7+8 = 20$. The number left over is 6.

**Answer: (D) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-20.title: Count all colourings
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-20.body:
All three colours must be used, so head, wings and tail get three different colours. The head can be any of 3 colours, the wings one of the 2 others, and the tail gets the last one: $3\times2\times1 = 6$ different parrots. One is already done, so she can colour $6 - 1 = 5$ more.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-20.title: List them
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-20.body:
(head, wings, tail): RGB (done), RBG, GRB, GBR, BRG, BGR — 5 more.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-21.title: Where are the three books?
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-21.body:
The largest book is in position 21 from the left. The oldest book is next to both, so the smallest and the largest are 2 places apart with the oldest between them.

To keep the shelf short, put the smallest book to the **left**: smallest at 19, oldest at 20, largest at 21. Then there are 22 books to the right of position 19, so the shelf has $19 + 22 = 41$ books.

(If the smallest were at position 23, we would need $23 + 22 = 45$ books.)

**Answer: (B) 41**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-21.title: Count around the group
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-21.body:
Think of the group of three books (smallest, oldest, largest). Left of the largest: 20 books = 2 books of the group + 18 others. Right of the smallest: 22 books = 2 books of the group + 20 others. Total: $18 + 3 + 20 = 41$.

**Answer: (B) 41**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-22.title: Start from the stem of (B)
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-22.body:
Each shape has 15 squares, so each part has 5 squares.

In (B), look at the bottom of the stem: the lowest square and the square sticking out to the left can only join the part through the stem square between them. That part then needs two more squares, and the only way is straight up the stem to the ring. So one part is forced: the whole stem (5 squares).

What is left is the ring of 8 squares with one extra square at the top-left and one at the bottom-right. This leftover shape looks exactly the same after a half turn, and each of the two parts must contain one extra square plus 4 ring squares. However you cut the ring, the half turn carries one part onto the other, so the two parts always have the **same** shape. So (B) cannot be cut into three different parts.

The other shapes can be cut into three different parts (try it: start from the bottom of each stem).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-22.title: Why symmetry matters
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-22.body:
In (B) the stem is forced to be one part. The remaining 10 squares form a figure with half-turn symmetry, where both extra squares must be in different parts (a part containing both would need 7 squares). The only cuts are into two 'mirror-turned' halves, which are copies of each other. In (A), (C), (D) and (E) the leftover is not symmetric like this, and the parts can be chosen to be different.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-23.title: Make each part as good as possible
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-23.body:
There are 6 different letters K, A, N, R, O, G, so 1–6 are each used once.

- K is the hundreds of the number we add: K = 6.
- R is the hundreds of the number we subtract: R = 1.
- O appears twice in the subtracted number ROO: make it small, O = 2.
- A is tens in KAN **and** ones in GA (worth 11), G is tens in GA (worth 10), N is ones (worth 1). So A = 5, G = 4, N = 3.

$653 - 122 + 45 = 576$.

**Answer: (C) 576**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-23.title: Value of each letter
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-23.body:
Write the result by place value: $\text{KAN} - \text{ROO} + \text{GA} = 100K + 11A + 10G + N - 100R - 11O$. Give the biggest numbers to the letters with the biggest plus-values and the smallest to the biggest minus-values: $K = 6$, $A = 5$, $G = 4$, $N = 3$, and $R = 1$, $O = 2$ (R is worth more, so it gets the smallest number). Result: $600 + 55 + 40 + 3 - 100 - 22 = 576$.

**Answer: (C) 576**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-24.title: Look at the folds
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-24.body:
When the strip is folded into a pile, the connections 1–2, 2–3 and 3–4 become folds on the left or right side of the pile. Cell 2 has its two folds on opposite sides, and so does cell 3. So folds 1–2 and 3–4 are on the **same** side, and 2–3 is on the other.

Two folds on the same side cannot cross each other: one must be inside the other or they must be apart.

In (D) the order is 3, 1, 4, 2 (layers 1 to 4). Fold 1–2 joins layers 2 and 4; fold 3–4 joins layers 1 and 3. These overlap like links of a chain — they would have to cross. Impossible.

For (A) 3, 1, 2, 4: fold 1–2 joins layers 2 and 3, which sits inside fold 3–4 (layers 1 and 4) — fine.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-24.title: Try it with a paper strip
kangaroo-ca-2020-g0304-24.body:
Make a strip of 4 squares, number them and try. You can get 3,1,2,4 (fold 1 onto 2, then roll 3 on top and 4 under), 3,4,2,1, 3,2,1,4 and 3,4,1,2, but in 3,1,4,2 the paper would have to pass through itself.

**Answer: (D)**
